# Introduction

Sickle cell disease (SCD) can involve painful vaso-occlusive episodes, and air pollution may aggravate these outcomes. This exploratory report summarizes ambient carbon monoxide (CO), fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and ozone (O3) measured at the EPA monitor at RDU airport. These environmental data alone do not establish associations with individual SCD outcomes.

# Data preparation

The input comprises daily monitor records for 2018, 2019, and January–April 2020. Exact duplicate records are removed, negative readings are replaced with zero, and multiple readings for the same day are averaged separately for each pollutant. Missing measurements are omitted from pollutant-specific calculations.

```{r processing}
#' Read and clean one year of RDU air-quality observations.
#' @param file_path Path to one annual CSV file.
#' @param ozone_units Desired ozone units: "ppm" (default) or "ppb".
#' @return Tibble with one row per date and cleaned daily mean pollutant values.
process_air_quality <- function(file_path, ozone_units = "ppm") {
  ozone_units <- match.arg(ozone_units, c("ppm", "ppb"))
  x <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(Date = mdy(Date),
              CO_ppm = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
              PM25_ug_m3 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
              O3_ppm = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`) %>%
    distinct()
  pollutants <- c("CO_ppm", "PM25_ug_m3", "O3_ppm")
  for (pollutant in pollutants) {
    x[[pollutant]] <- ifelse(!is.na(x[[pollutant]]) & x[[pollutant]] < 0,
                            0, x[[pollutant]])
  }
  x <- x %>% group_by(Date) %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(pollutants),
                     ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
              .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(Date)
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") x <- x %>% mutate(O3_ppm = O3_ppm * 1000) %>%
    rename(O3_ppb = O3_ppm)
  x
}

air_quality <- bind_rows(lapply(2018:2020, function(yr) {
  process_air_quality(file.path("data", paste0("AQ_", yr, ".csv"))) %>%
    mutate(year = yr)
})) %>% mutate(month = month(Date))
```

# Annual concentration ranges

The following tables give the minimum and maximum **daily** concentration for each year, after cleaning and averaging repeated daily measurements.

```{r tables, results='asis'}
for (yr in 2018:2020) {
  summary_table <- air_quality %>% filter(year == yr) %>%
    summarise(across(c(CO_ppm, PM25_ug_m3, O3_ppm),
                     list(Min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), Max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("Pollutant", ".value"), names_pattern = "(.*)_(Min|Max)$") %>%
    mutate(Pollutant = recode(Pollutant,
      CO_ppm = "CO (ppm)", PM25_ug_m3 = "PM2.5 (ug/m3)", O3_ppm = "O3 (ppm)"))
  cat("\n\n### ", yr, " daily concentration ranges\n\n", sep="")
  print(knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 3,
       col.names = c("Pollutant", "Minimum", "Maximum")))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Monthly patterns

```{r plot1, fig.cap="Figure 1. Pooled daily monthly means and normal-approximation 95% confidence intervals for CO and ozone."}
monthly <- air_quality %>%
  pivot_longer(c(CO_ppm, O3_ppm), names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)), mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lower = mean - 1.96 * sd / sqrt(n),
         upper = mean + 1.96 * sd / sqrt(n),
         pollutant = recode(pollutant, CO_ppm = "CO (ppm)", O3_ppm = "Ozone (ppm)"))
ggplot(monthly, aes(month, mean, color = pollutant)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .18) +
  geom_point(size = 2.3) + geom_line(linewidth = .5) +
  facet_wrap(~pollutant, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CO (ppm)" = "#187b91", "Ozone (ppm)" = "#d27435")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly CO and ozone (2018–2020)", x = "Month", y = "Daily concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

CO and ozone use separate panels with free y-axis scales because their concentration ranges differ substantially. This preserves their original ppm units and makes both seasonal patterns visible without implying that their magnitudes are directly comparable.

```{r plot2, fig.cap="Figure 2. Mean daily PM2.5 concentration by calendar month and year."}
pm_monthly <- air_quality %>% group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(mean_pm = mean(PM25_ug_m3, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pm_monthly, aes(month, mean_pm, color = factor(year), group = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .8) + geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2018" = "#187b91", "2019" = "#d27435", "2020" = "#7663a7")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly PM2.5 by year", x = "Month", y = "PM2.5 (ug/m3)", color = "Year") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

A line-and-point plot emphasizes month-to-month changes and allows year-to-year comparisons without displaying hundreds of overlapping daily observations. The 2020 series appropriately ends in April.

# Interpretation

Ozone concentrations tend to rise in the warmer months, while CO generally shows higher concentrations during cooler months. PM2.5 fluctuates across months and years rather than following a perfectly consistent seasonal pattern; the 2020 series should not be compared as a full year because it contains only January–April data.
